newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra bill progresses in Australian Senate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra bill progresses in Australian Senate.

text.p: The bill to partially privatise telecoms carrier Telstra overcame a hurdle in the Australian Senate on Thursday, progressing from the debate stage to the stage where it might be amended.
The bill, which will pass by a bare majority, if at all might have been rejected on that vote.
The bill passed that hurdle on a vote of 35 to 33 thanks to key Independent senators Mal Colston and Brian Harradine supporting the government.
Both, however, could reverse their vote at a later stage.

Shortly before the vote, the government sweetened its lure for the Independents, increasing the environmental repair fund it promises to set up with Telstra proceeds to A$1.1 billion from A$1.0 billion.
It also promised a new A$250 million fund to develop telecommunications infrastructure outside of main cities.

Immediately after the vote, one of the non-government parties opposed to the sale, the Democrats, moved to delay the bill until next year, and at 0045 GMT (11.45 a.m.) the Senate was sidetracked on that motion.
The government is hoping for a final vote on Thursday.
Both Independents have signalled they could support the partial sale of Telstra if certain conditions are met.
Colston said he expected his concerns to be met and believed the government had a mandate for the sale.
"It is hard to argue that the coalition did not obtain a mandate to sell one-third of Telstra," Colston told parliament earlier on Thursday.
Harradine said his negotiations with the government had gone well on most issues, although he remained concerned about the method by which the telecoms carrier would be sold.
"If all of those matters were satisfactorily concluded, I would believe I would be doing my duty in voting for the (bill)," he told parliament.
The government hopes to raise A$8.0 billion from the partial sale of Telstra. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
